@graph.name: Thermoformed Package Case Packer
@graph.description: A thermoformed package case packer is a top-load machine that picks sealed thermoformed packages, such as meat, cheese or prepared food packs, and places them into shipping cases in a set pattern. TRF Industrial Automation packs thermoformed packages with TRFRapidpack and TRFOnepack. Which one fits is defined mainly by your line setup and speed.

mainEntity.name: Can a Robotic Case Packer Handle Pouches, Trays and Thermoformed Packages in the Same Line?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, within the validated application. TRFRapidpack packs pouches, pillow bags, flow packs, thermoformed packages, trays, cartons, cups and tubs, and it changes products and patterns by recipe with reduced mechanical adjustments. Each package format, pick tool and pattern is validated during project engineering, so share every format the line will run before the system is specified.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Difference Between an Integrated Case Packer and Separate Erecting, Packing and Sealing Machines?

acceptedAnswer.text: An integrated case packer erects the case, loads it and seals it in one coordinated machine, with one controls platform. Separate machines each need their own interfaces, controls and floor space. TRFOnepack is the integrated option, for applications of about 20 to 50 products per minute, and it can start standalone and later join a complete TRF end-of-line system.

mainEntity.name: What Floor Space Does an Integrated Case Packing Machine Require?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the case size, the pack pattern, the infeed and how operators reach the machine. What changes the answer most is consolidation: TRFOnepack combines case erecting, robotic packing and case sealing in one machine architecture, which takes less floor space than three machines in series. TRF places the machine in your floor plan, with infeed and discharge, during the application review.

mainEntity.name: How Many Products per Minute Can a Robotic Case Packer Run?

acceptedAnswer.text: TRFRapidpack is designed for applications of about 100 to 200 products per minute. TRF publishes application ranges, not machine speeds: actual capacity depends on the package, the pick tool, the pack pattern and how packages leave the thermoformer, and TRF engineering validates it for each line before the design is closed.

mainEntity.name: Can Case Packing Equipment Integrate With My Existing Palletizer and Conveyors?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Each TRF case packing platform can run standalone or integrate with conveyors, case handling, palletizing and intralogistics as one end-of-line system. The signals and buffers between your thermoformer and the case packer, and the handoff to a TRFCobot, TRFCompact or TRFSpeed palletizer, are defined during project engineering. See end-of-line integration.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Difference Between a Case Packer and a Case Erector?

acceptedAnswer.text: A case erector forms an open case from a flat blank, and a case packer loads products into that case. TRF supplies case erecting only as part of an integrated solution: TRFOnepack erects, packs and seals in one machine, and end-of-line projects with TRFRapidpack include case forming and closing, so one partner answers for the flow from flat case to sealed case.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Typical ROI of Switching From Manual to Robotic Case Packing?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no typical figure, because payback depends on your plant. The estimate compares the installed cost of the system with the annual savings: people packing cases on each shift, shifts per day, local labor cost, output the thermoformer gains when packing stops limiting it, packs damaged by handling and time saved at changeovers. A TRF Sales Engineer builds it with your data.
